text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Government budget talks should deal with costs arising from foreign-exchange fluctuations and lower interest rate expenses together -- not separately as Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto did, says economist Jukka Pekkarinen of Labour Institute of Economic Research.
- Swedish state-owned power producer Vattenfall has renewed its bid of 1.8 billion markka for regional Finnish power companies Savon Voima and Kuopion Energia.
- Government decision to change the system of calculating daily unemployment benefits favours jobless people who previously had high incomes, says Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).

- The government has tied its strategies to recent budget plan and upcoming pay talks; in doing so, it has silently approved massive unemployment and regional inequality, says Esko Aho, MP and leader of the main opposition Centre Party.

- A broad pay deal is possible even if the paper workers union does not participate; room should also be allowed for dealing with branch-specific problems, says Esa Swanljung, chairman of the Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK).
- The number of over-weight school children in Finland has doubled in 20 years, a medical study shows.

- Nokia's 2110 mobile phone radiates more than five other mobile phone models, Norwegian newspaper Dagbladet says based on a Swiss study. Company says radiation differences between phones insignificant because levels low.
KAUPPALEHTI
- After Wall Street's Friday slide, major investors on Helsinki stock exchange held back while mainly small investors grew jittery and sold shares.

- Investors hold only small amounts of membership certificates in cooperative Helsinki telephone company HPY, and the main owners are still the city of Helsinki and the state. Company says it will seek a bourse listing in September and membership certificates are expected to appreciate.
- Government plans to hike electricity and other energy tax by a billion markka to fund the cuts in income taxes.
- Insurance companies should participate in private funding of roads, Transport Minister Matti Aura says; insurance companies have showed interest.
AAMULEHTI
- Atmosphere for a broad pay deal is more positive than in the spring, trade union federation SAK says.
- Companies selling solar energy technology should be promoted, says head of oil group Neste's Advaced Power Systems unit.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish paper industry is taking part in EU-funded reseach project aiming to boost competitiveness of ageing industry.
DEMARI
- Significant sector-based agreements should be reached in the food industry before it can participate in a broad pay deal, food workers union spokesman says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
